answer:
HYPOTHESIS (natural-language answer to the question):

Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form first show opposite growth trends in the **18th century BCE, around 1700 BCE** (the transition between the 1800 BCE and 1700 BCE century bins of the dataset). In that interval, Pottery Decoration diversity rises sharply — from a z-score of −0.48 to **+0.97 (ΔDec = +1.45 z-units, ≈3.4 SD of its own historical century-to-century changes, SD ≈ 0.43)** — while Pottery Form diversity drops simultaneously from +0.74 to **−1.13 (ΔForm = −1.87 z-units)**, its lowest level in the entire 4300–500 BCE record. This is the **only** century in the whole series where Decoration increases and Form declines simultaneously (even under the loosest criterion — any Decoration rise with any Form decline — no other bin qualifies), and it coincides with the transition out of the Late Neolithic (LN) into the Bronze-Age OBA/YBA groups in the capital.csv period labels. Interpreted archaeologically: as vessel-form diversity collapsed into a standardized repertoire, potters shifted expressive effort into surface ornamentation — a divergent style strategy rather than co-varying diversity — marking a reorganization of ceramic production (standardization of form paired with elaboration of decoration) from roughly the 18th century BCE onward, persisting through 500 BCE.

Century-naming note (ambiguity handled explicitly): the dataset's century bin labeled **1700 BCE** (CE −1700, calBP 3200) spans 1700–1601 BCE, which is conventionally the **17th century BCE**; the transition itself unfolds during the **18th century BCE (1800–1701 BCE)**, and the annual smoothed-derivative check places the first opposite-trend crossing at ~CE −1800 with the shift complete by the 1700 BCE bin. Thus the answer is "around 1700 BCE — the 18th/17th-century-BCE transition," with the 1700 BCE bin being the first century-level observation exhibiting the opposite configuration.

CAVEATS: (1) "Significant" here means the pre-stated deterministic threshold (ΔDec ≥ +0.5 z-units, sensitivity-checked at >1 SD of historical changes = 0.43), NOT a formal statistical test — the series are z-scores without an error model. (2) The Form decline is a one-time level shift: Form plateaus at exactly −1.13 from 1700 BCE to 500 BCE, so "declining simultaneously" strictly holds at the transition, not as a sustained slope. (3) The annual `_inter` series is an exact linear interpolation of the 37 century values, so intra-century "trends" (e.g., the ~1800 BCE crossing) are interpolation artifacts of the underlying step change. (4) Diversity here is proxied by standardized z-scores of pottery-form and pottery-decoration frequency measures, not direct diversity indices.

answer_summary.first_bin: CE -1700 (1700 BCE bin; spans 1700-1601 BCE = conventionally the 17th century BCE; transition unfolds during the 18th century BCE 1800-1701 BCE)

payload.hypothesis: Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form first show opposite growth trends in the 18th century BCE, around 1700 BCE: Pottery Decoration diversity rises sharply (z-score -0.48 to +0.97, delta = +1.45, about 3.4 SD of its historical century-to-century variability) while Pottery Form diversity drops simultaneously to its lowest recorded level (+0.74 to -1.13, delta = -1.87). This is the only century in the entire 4300-500 BCE record where Decoration increases and Form declines simultaneously, coinciding with the Late Neolithic-to-Bronze-Age (LN to OBA) cultural transition. Archaeologically, this marks a reorganization of ceramic production: vessel forms became standardized (form diversity collapsing to a plateau of -1.13 lasting to 500 BCE) while decorative diversity was elaborated to its maximum (+0.97 to +1.53), i.e., a divergent style strategy in which standardized shapes were differentiated through surface ornamentation.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE -4100..-500). Extracted the 37 century bins where raw PotteryDecoration/PotteryForm z-scores are observed; verified _inter series are exact linear interpolations (max residual 2.2e-16) and identical to raw on the century grid. Computed century-to-century changes dDec and dForm; scanned chronologically from 4300 BCE for the first bin with dDec >= +0.5 z-units AND dForm < 0 (sensitivity: dDec >= 1 SD of changes = 0.431; loosest: any Decoration rise). Triangulated with a 100-year rolling smoothed derivative of the annual _inter series (opposite-trend window CE -1800..-1601, centered on the 1700 BCE bin). Cross-validated all 37 century values against capital.csv (exact match, max |diff| = 0), including cultural period labels (LN to OBA transition). Thresholds are deterministic decision rules, not statistical tests (z-scores without an error model).
